item.title: Dunwoody Park getting new ADA-accessible playground this winter
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola's Parks and Recreation Department has finalized designs for a replacement playground at Dunwoody Park, with work expected to wrap up by winter 2026. The decision comes after public input gathered in early July, when the city hosted a design session ahead of the Fourth of July Kids Bike Parade in the Cordova Park neighborhood. Residents…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola's Parks and Recreation Department has finalized designs for a replacement playground at Dunwoody Park, with work expected to wrap up by winter 2026.

The decision comes after public input gathered in early July, when the city hosted a design session ahead of the Fourth of July Kids Bike Parade in the Cordova Park neighborhood. Residents were shown two playground options, both featuring ADA-accessible features, and asked for feedback through a survey.

The project was developed in collaboration with District 4 City Councilman Jared Moore. The city said the new playground will replace the existing equipment at the park.

item.title: Florida's Final Minimum Wage Hike Kicks In October 1
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A batch of new Florida laws take effect October 1, including the final $1 increase in the state's voter-approved minimum wage push. The hike, which has been phased in over several years following voter approval, will bring Florida's minimum wage to $15 per hour. Alongside the wage increase, several other laws debut next month that could affect…
item.content:encoded:
A batch of new Florida laws take effect October 1, including the final $1 increase in the state's voter-approved minimum wage push. The hike, which has been phased in over several years following voter approval, will bring Florida's minimum wage to $15 per hour.

Alongside the wage increase, several other laws debut next month that could affect Northwest Florida residents and businesses. Police will operate under new guidelines for identifying criminal gang members, while lawmakers have created a new penalty specifically targeting anyone who involves minors in animal fighting—a significant expansion of animal cruelty enforcement.

Drivers should also take note of clarifications to license plate frame rules that take effect the same day. The changes are part of a larger slate of legislation that passed during the 2026 session.

item.content:encoded:
If you want to get your group, business, or organization in Northview High School's homecoming parade next month, you've got until Thursday to sign up.

The parade is set for October 2, with registration closing at the end of Thursday, September 24. Entry is free, and organizers say you can grab the entry form and release online to get submitted before the deadline hits.

The parade itself will line up at noon and start rolling at 12:30 p.m. from Northview High School. Whether you're representing a local business, a student club, or just want to be part of the festivities, now's the time to get your entry in.

item.content:encoded:
North Escambia is in for some nice weather as the area settles into fall conditions. Tuesday evening's sunset painted the sky in dramatic colors across the region, with vibrant displays visible from Tate High School's sports fields to rural Molino, and a rainbow stretching across Highway 29 in Cantonment.

The pleasant conditions are expected to continue in the coming days, with sunny skies and mild temperatures forecast for the area. It's the kind of weather that has locals stepping outside to catch the seasonal transition—and Tuesday's dramatic sunset showed why.

Tate High School welcomed three dozen new students into the National Honor Society this week, recognizing their achievement across the organization's core values. Membership in the prestigious academic organization requires demonstrated excellence in scholarship, service, leadership, and character—a combination that school officials say reflects the caliber of student leaders at the North Escambia campus.

The National Honor Society has long served as a marker of academic distinction and civic commitment among high school students. Induction into the organization is typically competitive, with students needing to maintain strong GPAs and demonstrate meaningful contributions to their school and community.

While specific details about individual inductees were not immediately available, the induction of 36 new members suggests a strong showing of academic and civic achievement at Tate this school year.

item.title: Escambia Schools vows prosecution after Ransom Middle bomb threat
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Public Schools officials say they're pursuing criminal charges after a bomb threat forced delays at Ransom Middle School on Tuesday. The district emphasized that disruptive hoaxes targeting schools will not go unpunished and pledged to work with law enforcement to seek full prosecution in the case. The threat, which officials…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Public Schools officials say they're pursuing criminal charges after a bomb threat forced delays at Ransom Middle School on Tuesday. The district emphasized that disruptive hoaxes targeting schools will not go unpunished and pledged to work with law enforcement to seek full prosecution in the case.

The threat, which officials characterized as a 'bot' hoax, disrupted the start of the school day. No injuries were reported, and no explosive device was found, according to the district's statement.

District leaders made clear that threats against schools—whether genuine or false—carry serious consequences. "We will not tolerate disruptive behavior that puts our students and staff at risk or disrupts their education," school officials said in their Tuesday statement.

The incident marks another reminder of the ongoing challenge schools face with threat-related disruptions. The district did not immediately release additional details about the investigation or identify suspects.

The election also decided the race for City Council seat 1, though detailed results…
item.content:encoded:
Frisco City held a special municipal election Tuesday that determined both the mayor's office and a City Council seat. Current Mayor Brandaun Love secured reelection, defeating challenger Allen Lang with 266 votes compared to Lang's 87, according to WKRG News 5.

The election also decided the race for City Council seat 1, though detailed results for that contest were not immediately available. Love will continue in the mayor's role following his victory.

The special election gave Frisco City voters a chance to weigh in on municipal leadership in the Monroe County community.

item.title: Calm evening conditions on Pensacola Bay as tide rises
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Light winds and modest wave action characterized Pensacola's waterfront Wednesday evening, with conditions favorable for outdoor activities along the Gulf Coast. According to Florida Gulf Signal, air temperatures held at nearly 84 degrees with gentle 7.8-knot easterly winds pushing waves just over a foot high. Tide activity showed high water at…
item.content:encoded:
Light winds and modest wave action characterized Pensacola's waterfront Wednesday evening, with conditions favorable for outdoor activities along the Gulf Coast. According to Florida Gulf Signal, air temperatures held at nearly 84 degrees with gentle 7.8-knot easterly winds pushing waves just over a foot high.

Tide activity showed high water at 1.6 feet early this morning around 9:17 a.m., with the next low tide expected at 7:18 p.m. bringing levels down to 0.6 feet. The gradual tidal swing creates typical mid-week conditions for the Panhandle.

Those planning evening beach or waterfront outings can expect calm seas and comfortable temperatures, though light winds may make it a slower evening for water sports enthusiasts.

item.title: Gusty Thunderstorm Winds Hit NAS Pensacola Tuesday Afternoon
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A strong thunderstorm swept across NAS Pensacola on Tuesday afternoon, producing wind gusts up to 41 miles per hour, according to the automated weather station at the base. The National Weather Service recorded the peak gust at 4:19 p.m. CDT at AWOS station KNPA on the naval air station. The marine thunderstorm wind advisory flagged winds…
item.content:encoded:
A strong thunderstorm swept across NAS Pensacola on Tuesday afternoon, producing wind gusts up to 41 miles per hour, according to the automated weather station at the base.

The National Weather Service recorded the peak gust at 4:19 p.m. CDT at AWOS station KNPA on the naval air station. The marine thunderstorm wind advisory flagged winds equivalent to 36 knots as the system moved through Escambia County.

While the gust was notable, it fell short of warning thresholds that would trigger broader alerts across the region. No damage reports were immediately available from the base or surrounding areas.
